clue.text: Some attend lessons non-stop

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some pupils go to class without a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Something non-stop goes on without ever finishing, which is what endless means.

clue.text: Old big case

parts.note: ex means former or old
ample means big or generous

explanation.surface: An elderly large suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: A case is an instance, and an example is one instance cited to illustrate.

clue.text: Moving picture

definitions.meaning: moving in the sense of pulling along, as a horse moves a cart
a sketch or illustration made with pencil or pen

explanation.surface: A film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving picture' reads as a cinema film, but it splits into two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing is pulling something along, and a drawing is a picture made with lines.

clue.text: Still time for item in a sports programme

parts.note: still can mean even, as in still better or even better

explanation.surface: There is yet time for one more fixture in the schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Each race or contest on a sports programme is called an event.

clue.text: Most rum gets Stan drunk? That's about right

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the right letter
drunk suggests something reeling and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Stan gets drunk on the oddest rum, and someone agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges GETS STAN into STANGEST, and 'about' wraps it round R. Rum is British for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is an old British word for odd, so most rum means oddest, a superlative.

clue.text: Cobblers totter after client, finally

indicators.note: after places the walking word behind the closing letter of client
finally asks for only the closing letter of the word client

parts.note: to totter is to walk unsteadily, to waddle

explanation.surface: A cobbler's shop where a customer wobbles out after being served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts WADDLE behind T, the last letter of client. Cobblers is British slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobblers is British slang for rubbish talk, a synonym of nonsense or twaddle.

clue.text: You might ride on these tense animals

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
rams are male sheep, animals

explanation.surface: Nervy beasts that people ride.
explanation.definitionFit: Trams are streetcars that passengers ride along city rails.

clue.text: Bold and decisive vet raises cuckoo

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters go mad and rearrange

explanation.surface: A vet confidently rears a cuckoo chick.
explanation.definitionFit: An assertive person is confident and forceful, bold and decisive in manner.

clue.text: Cover upside down on novel, creating quandary

indicators.note: upside down in a down clue means the lid letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: a lid is a cover
Emma is the novel by Jane Austen

explanation.surface: A book cover printed upside down causes a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upside down' reverses the cover word, which in a down entry sits on top of the Jane Austen title; 'creating' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a difficult choice between alternatives, a quandary.

clue.text: Leave the seedy hotel's scrubbed lift

indicators.note: seedy means shabby and disreputable, a sign the letters are in a mess
scrubbed means cancelled, so the hotel letter is removed

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Get out of the run-down hotel, cleaned out of its elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrubbed' takes H out of LEAVE THE, leaving LEAVETE, and 'seedy' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate is to raise up, the verb sense of lift.

clue.text: Incompetent American mother pressing uniform

indicators.note: pressing pictures the mother word squeezing the uniform letter inside her

parts.note: mater is Latin, and old British schoolboy slang, for mother
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American mum who is hopeless at ironing a uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressing' puts U inside MATER, giving MATEUR after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur, used disparagingly, is an unskilled or inept performer.

clue.text: Free bishop stuck in a crack

indicators.note: stuck in places the bishop letter inside the run formed by a and the cracking word

parts.note: to crack a problem is to solve it
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A clergyman is freed after getting wedged in a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck in' puts B between A and SOLVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to set them free of guilt or obligation, a verb sense of free.

clue.text: What we got from Constable sniping at criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A police constable taking potshots at a lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Constable looks like a police officer but is John Constable, the English landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable left us canvases such as The Hay Wain, so his works are the output described.

clue.text: Polish nurses beginning to master a dance

indicators.note: nurses means holds or cradles, so the polishing word holds a letter inside

parts.note: to polish is to rub

indicators.note: beginning to asks for the opening letter of master

explanation.surface: Shining shoes while looking after the start of a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' puts M (from 'beginning to master') inside RUB; the A is the clue's own 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Latin American ballroom dance of Cuban origin.

clue.text: Regularly recap golfer's score of two under par

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the words that follow, here the even ones

explanation.surface: Periodically summarising how a golfer is doing on the card.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a hole completed in two strokes fewer than par is called an eagle.

clue.text: Former lover on X — derisive but not half profound

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
X is the Roman numeral for ten

indicators.note: not half means losing half the word, here its first four letters

explanation.surface: An ex sneers at an X with a deep scorn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' drops DERI from derisive, leaving SIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Extensive means wide-ranging or thorough, a sense close to deep or profound.

clue.text: Get rid of priest pal entertains at home

parts.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

indicators.note: entertains means has as a guest, so the pal word holds another inside

parts.note: a mate is a pal
in means at home

explanation.surface: A clergyman's friend has visitors round to the house.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli is the Old Testament priest of Shiloh; 'entertains' has the pal word host the at-home word, as a guest is held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate something is to remove it entirely, an exact synonym of get rid of.

clue.text: Suggested Charlie enters country with Ted

indicators.note: enters means goes into, so the Charlie letter goes inside the country

parts.note: India is a country
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hinted that Charlie travels to a nation with his friend Ted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' places Charlie inside the country; Ted simply follows, joined by 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have indicated something is to have pointed to or suggested it.

clue.text: New AI test he'd paused

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A man stopped before trying out a novel artificial intelligence check.
explanation.definitionFit: To have hesitated is to have paused briefly before acting.

clue.text: Rider possibly hollow-eyed and gaunt

definitions.meaning: H. Rider ... is the English author of King Solomon's Mines

explanation.definitionFit: The novelist H Rider Haggard bears the surname, and haggard means drawn and exhausted.

clue.text: Look around bottom of barrel for a kipper

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the look word goes round the barrel letter

parts.note: to see is to look

indicators.note: bottom of asks for the last letter of barrel, the base in a down clue

parts.note: per means for a, as in ten pence per item

explanation.surface: Checking the bottom of a barrel to find a smoked fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts L inside SEE. A kipper is a smoked herring, but here one who kips, British slang for sleeps.
explanation.definitionFit: To kip is British slang for to sleep, so a kipper is someone sleeping.

clue.text: Support for artist's adult son catching fish? Just the opposite

indicators.note: catching would put the fish inside the adult and son letters
just the opposite reverses who catches whom, so the fish holds them instead

parts.note: an eel is a fish
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: An artist's grown-up boy lands a fish for his stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' alone would put EEL inside AS; 'Just the opposite' flips it, so EEL holds AS.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the stand that holds an artist's canvas while painting.

clue.text: Nick criticised short king

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: slammed means harshly criticised
R is rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone panned a king for being short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the D from SLAMMED. Nick is British slang for a prison, as is slammer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick and slammer are both slang words for a prison or jail.

clue.text: Large motorboats dropping off ace meals

indicators.note: dropping off means shedding, so the ace letter is removed

parts.note: launches are motorboats
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: Big boats losing their best crew at mealtimes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping off' removes A from LAUNCHES, leaving LUNCHES after L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunches are midday meals.

clue.text: Naive politician

definitions.meaning: naive means inexperienced or gullible, like a raw beginner
a member of an environmentalist party such as the ... Party

explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced, and a Green is a politician from an ecology party.

clue.text: Not sure about boring irate nun, unfortunately

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the about letter goes into the rearranged letters
unfortunately suggests things go wrong, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Doubtful about a tedious, angry nun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges IRATE NUN to UNERTAIN, and 'boring' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncertain means lacking confidence or doubtful, a straight synonym of not sure.

clue.text: Distress from pressure after university class

indicators.note: after puts the pressure letter behind the university letter

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
a set is a class or group, as in a school set

explanation.surface: A student is distressed by exam stress after a lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset someone is to distress them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Checks rules for the audience

indicators.note: for the audience means as heard by listeners, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a monarch reigns, or rules

explanation.surface: An umpire checks the regulations for spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: REIGNS sounds like REINS.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein something in is to restrain it, so reins as a verb means checks.

clue.text: Fruit sandwiches one brings to bear

indicators.note: sandwiches means puts between layers, so the fruit holds a letter inside

parts.note: apples are fruit
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fruit sandwich being brought to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' puts I inside APPLES.
explanation.definitionFit: To apply pressure or force is to bring it to bear, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Jubilation from president repressing international hopes, primarily

indicators.note: repressing pictures the president word holding another letter down inside

parts.note: Donald Trump is a US president

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of hopes

explanation.surface: A leader's joy at crushing global aspirations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repressing' puts I inside TRUMP; 'primarily' adds H from hopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Triumph is the joy or elation felt at a victory, matching jubilation.

clue.text: Shoot gripping Ken Loach film that's most sinister

indicators.note: gripping means holding tightly, so the shoot word holds the film title inside

parts.note: to dart is to shoot or dash
Kes is Ken Loach's 1969 film about a boy and his kestrel

explanation.surface: Filming a gripping Ken Loach movie that turns out very dark.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Loach is a British director of social-realist films; 'gripping' has the shoot word hold his best-known title.
explanation.definitionFit: Darkest means most evil or menacing, the superlative of dark in its sinister sense.

clue.text: Education reflected father's wishes

indicators.note: reflected means seen in a mirror, so the education letters are turned backwards

parts.note: a sire is a father, and the 's becomes the final S

explanation.surface: Schooling mirrored what a dad wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns ED into DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Desires as a plural noun are things longed for, the same as wishes.
